scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: Campus 2 here, and both of our floors are broken at
the same time: the people on 10.5.0.x and the people on 10.6.0.x cannot
get to their gateway things -- 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 -- and it has
been like this since some reload earlier. Two floors losing their gateways
at once after a reload is not a coincidence, and it is not us. I won't
pretend to know what those boxes are, but they are yours. Find out why
both floors lost their gateways and put it right today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that hosts on 10.5.0.x and 10.6.0.x cannot reach their
default gateways (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 respectively) — does not exist in
the live network. All direct tests returned 0% packet loss.

The gateways are hosted on sshswitch as bridge interfaces br_v5 (10.5.0.254/24)
and br_v6 (10.6.0.254/24). These are fully UP. switch4 correctly bridges the
VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 access ports (eth1–eth6) to 802.1q sub-interfaces (eth0.5 and
eth0.6) on the trunk link (ms1_sw4) connecting to sshswitch's eth0.5/eth0.6,
which land in br_v5 and br_v6 respectively. MAC learning is functioning in both
directions on switch4 and sshswitch: all end-host MACs appear in the correct
bridge FDB entries. ARP resolution on both sshswitch and the PCs is correct.
There are no iptables or ebtables rules on sshswitch that could block traffic.
The uplink from sshswitch to router17 (bond0 ↔ 55.5.1.x) is UP with zero
errors and carries OSPF routes correctly. Cross-subnet reachability from VLAN 5
hosts through the gateway to router17 (55.5.1.1) also works.

Root cause: There is no fault. The ticket's premise is incorrect — the network
was and is healthy for VLANs 5 and 6. The "reload" mentioned by the caller
likely caused a brief transient period (ARP/FDB caches unpopulated immediately
after boot) that self-resolved within seconds. No corrective action is needed on
any device.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs (10.5.0.254 / 10.6.0.254) are up and answer hosts with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states the sshswitch SVIs (br_v5 10.5.0.254 and br_v6 10.6.0.254) are fully UP and that all direct tests returned 0% packet loss.

The agent's investigation logs contain direct, relevant measurements (pings from PCs and sshswitch, bridge/ARP/FDB outputs, ip link states, iptables) that support the conclusion the SVIs and host→gateway paths are healthy. The reasoning consistently follows from those observations and the checks cover the essential diagnostics to rule out the reported fault.
